subject: Notification obligations & evidence access — clarifying exemptions and cooperation
messages:
From: Sarah Lively <sarah.lively@finovate.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finovate.com, legal@finovate.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Notification obligations under DPA - Finovate Payments

Hi Lauren / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We surfaced a limited security event tied to a misconfigured ingest bucket used by one of our sandbox integrations with Redwood. At this stage our internal triage shows limited exposure to PII (names + email hashes) from test accounts but we need to confirm scope and how Redwood will treat notification obligations under the DPA.

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm what your contract/DPA requires for initial notification timing (acknowledgement vs materiality notification)?
- Will Redwood limit cross-border transfers for forensic analysis unless legally compelled? We have EU users in-scope and want clarity on transfers to the US for investigation.

We'd also like to see an evidence-handover sample (how snapshots/log extracts are shared, retention guarantees). Attached is a short incident summary from our SREs.

We need a written response within 48 hours if possible so we can brief our board counsel. If helpful, we can set a quick call.

Regards,
Sarah
Security Operations
Finovate Payments

[Attachment: finovate_security_summary.txt (text)]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lively <sarah.lively@finovate.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notification obligations under DPA - Finovate Payments

Sarah — thanks for the summary and the clear asks. Appreciate the heads up. Short answer: we aim to be cooperative and avoid unnecessary cross-border movement of data; we also want a pragmatic timeline that balances rapid acknowledgement with factual confirmation.

High level proposal from Redwood (we can formalize in an MAP):
- Acknowledgement: we will send an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of receipt of a customer notification explaining the next steps and point of contact.
- Preliminary assessment: within 48 hours we will provide a preliminary scope (affected product surface, indicative user count, and whether the exposure appears to be PII as defined by the DPA).
- Formal notification: if the incident meets the DPA materiality threshold, we will issue a written notification (and a proposed remediation/mitigation plan) within 72 hours of the first notice.

Notes on transfers & evidence:
- Forensic analysis: our preference is to perform analysis in-region where feasible. If a US-based forensic snapshot is required, we will seek to minimize data transferred and use a custodian/proxy access method (redacted snapshot, limited TTL access).
- Legal compulsion: we will not rely on a unilateral "law enforcement" exemption to avoid customer notifications except where a binding legal order prevents disclosure; in those cases we will notify the customer to the extent permitted and escalate to our legal team.
- Logs & retention: we can provide audit logs and signed hashes for exported artifacts; we maintain per-customer telemetry for 90 days by default and can discuss extended retention for forensic purposes under an agreed MAP.

I've attached our current notify matrix for quick reference. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to align on the MAP and any contract redlines your legal team would request?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_notify_matrix_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sarah Lively <sarah.lively@finovate.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, legal@finovate.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notification obligations under DPA - Finovate Payments

Thanks Lauren — that structure is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our counsel and infosec team:

1) Exemptions: our legal team is concerned about any contractual language that would allow Redwood to delay notification by asserting cooperation with law enforcement or similar exemptions. Can you confirm whether Redwood has standard language that preserves the customer's right to be notified promptly unless a court order prohibits disclosure?

2) Scope proof: when you say "preliminary scope" within 48 hours, what evidence will be provided? Our minimum ask is: list of affected user IDs (hashed if necessary), affected endpoints, and a signed integrity hash of any snapshot you provide.

3) Subprocessor involvement: will Redwood be sharing any artifacts with subprocessors (for instance, a managed-forensics partner)? If so, what contractual assurances do subprocessors have around onward transfers and deletion timelines?

We can take the meeting — tomorrow afternoon works. I'll attach a short questionnaire so legal can document the answers.

Best,
Sarah

[Attachment: customer_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)]

Subject: Re: Notification obligations under DPA - Finovate Payments

Sarah — answers below and a suggested next step. Quoting your questions inline.

> 1) Exemptions: our legal team is concerned about any contractual language that would allow Redwood to delay notification by asserting cooperation with law enforcement or similar exemptions. Can you confirm whether Redwood has standard language that preserves the customer's right to be notified promptly unless a court order prohibits disclosure?

We do not include broad unilateral law-enforcement exceptions in our standard DPA that permit withholding notifications. Our standard language says we will notify customers promptly unless prohibited by a binding legal order; in such a case we will notify to the extent permitted and provide proof of the order to the customer’s counsel where lawfully permissible. We can provide the exact contract excerpt in tomorrow's call.

> 2) Scope proof: when you say "preliminary scope" within 48 hours, what evidence will be provided? Our minimum ask is: list of affected user IDs (hashed if necessary), affected endpoints, and a signed integrity hash of any snapshot you provide.

We can commit to the items you list for the preliminary scope. Operationally we will provide:
- Affected object types (example: user profiles, session tokens) and affected endpoints;
- Approximate count of affected customer IDs (we will hash where required);
- A signed SHA256 hash of any forensic snapshot or export;
- A short timeline of actions taken.

> 3) Subprocessor involvement: will Redwood be sharing any artifacts with subprocessors (for instance, a managed-forensics partner)? If so, what contractual assurances do subprocessors have around onward transfers and deletion timelines?

If we need a managed-forensics partner we will:
- Notify the customer before engaging the subprocessor (unless an emergency prevents prior notice) and provide subprocessor identity;
- Require subprocessors to abide by DPA-equivalent obligations (data use limited to investigation, deletion within agreed TTL, no onward transfers without customer consent except as legally required);
- Provide a short attestation describing contractual controls and deletion certificate after the engagement.

Next step: propose a 30-minute call tomorrow at 15:00 UTC to walk through the MAP and confirm any contract redlines. Ben (cc'ed) will join from legal and Vanessa will cover operations and evidence handling. If that slot doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

—Lauren
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
